answer: An agent economy can resist sybil farming with bank custody: each identity rents one safe-deposit box from a real bank, stores a catalogued relic appraised by an outside appraiser, and faces yearly in-person inspection. One renter, one box, one audit day: no parallel rush, no bulk discount. The custody fee doubles for each further box on the same funding trail, so the tenth fake costs another branch visit, another appraisal, and 512x the first fee. A shelf of fake boxes is no cheap oasis: the prism of bank custody splits every identity into real rent, real travel, and real outside money.
